done_state: A read-only facade opens the warehouse, checks v_atlas_status before answering anything (distinguishing never-run, failed-run, and checks-evaluated=0 from a genuinely clean run -- the vacuous-pass principle applied at this layer), refuses every request when the run is not genuinely clean with a reason naming which state it is in, and otherwise serves reads only from the declared set of gated views, never a raw table, matching ARCHITECTURE.md section 8's stated guarantee that primary enforcement of the trust gate lives here.

criteria.statement: The facade's connection to the warehouse is genuinely read-only -- a write attempt through it raises, not merely a convention the facade's own methods happen to honor.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_readonly.py: opens a facade against a migrated warehouse db, attempts an INSERT through the facade's own connection, asserts it raises sqlite3.OperationalError (SQLite's real read-only-connection error).

criteria.statement: status() returns a structured result distinguishing four states that must never collapse into each other: never-run (no ingest_run rows at all), a run whose own status is not 'ok', a run that IS 'ok' but recorded zero dq_check_run rows (checks_evaluated=0 -- the known vacuous-pass case), and a genuinely clean run (status='ok', checks_evaluated>0, contract_failures=0).
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_status.py: four separate fixtures, one per state, each asserting status() returns the correct, distinct classification -- most importantly that checks_evaluated=0 is never reported the same way as a genuine contract_failures=0 clean pass.

criteria.statement: fetch() only permits reading from the 18 views declared in ARCHITECTURE.md section 16 -- a request naming a raw table (e.g. hook_verdict directly) or any name outside that declared set is refused with a clear reason, never silently allowed.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: fetch('hook_verdict') and fetch('not_a_real_view') both raise a facade-specific refusal naming the requested name; fetch('v_gate_proven_live') against a clean run does not raise.

criteria.statement: When status() is not genuinely clean, fetch() refuses EVERY request (system-wide, not per-source) with a reason naming which of the three non-clean states applies -- extending section 8's per-source refusal with this component's own stronger, simpler policy, since the gated views already self-gate per-source at the SQL layer.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: for each of the three non-clean status() states, fetch() against a real, otherwise-valid view name raises a refusal whose message names that specific state, not a generic error.

criteria.statement: When the run is genuinely clean, fetch() against a real gated view returns rows identical to a direct SQL SELECT against the same view.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: loads a fixture with a clean run and real hook_verdict data, asserts facade.fetch('v_gate_proven_live') returns the same rows as a direct 'SELECT * FROM v_gate_proven_live' on the same connection.

failure_criteria.statement: fetch() returns data (or an empty result silently indistinguishable from 'no rows') when status() is not genuinely clean, rather than raising a distinguishable refusal.
failure_criteria.detection: Every non-clean status() state has its own fetch()-refuses test (C4); a refusal must be a raised, named exception type, never a quiet empty return.

failure_criteria.statement: A view/table count or allowlist size in this component's code comments or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: The facade assumes the warehouse database file exists and is a valid ATLAS schema, rather than reporting a named failure when it is missing or unmigrated.
failure_criteria.detection: Opening a facade against a nonexistent or unmigrated db path produces a named, observable error, not an unhandled exception with no context.

failure_criteria.statement: A refused query is logged to a channel nobody reads instead of being raised to the caller who can act on it.
failure_criteria.detection: Every refusal is a raised Python exception with a message the caller/test directly asserts on -- never a bare print or a swallowed condition.

out_of_scope: Foreman's periodic pattern-detection consumer itself (D12 in ARCHITECTURE.md) -- unbuilt and undesigned per the architecture document; this component only provides the read facade a future consumer would use.
The dashboard's specific query needs (D9) -- dashboard gets its own criteria once it is rewired against this facade.
Real end-to-end queries against the live warehouse populated by real ingest/resolve runs -- this component's tests use synthetic fixtures; end-to-end correctness is foreman:integration-test's job.
A general arbitrary-SQL escape hatch -- fetch() is restricted to the declared view allowlist by design (C3), not a general query() that accepts caller-supplied SQL against arbitrary tables.
constraints: Zero third-party dependencies -- Python 3 stdlib only (sqlite3), matching this environment's established convention.
The warehouse connection is opened in SQLite's real read-only URI mode (file:...?mode=ro), not merely a connection the facade's own code promises not to write through.
Tests use Python's stdlib unittest, matching every other component's own convention.
